card.occupation: Part-time graphic designer at a small independent print and signage firm in Stockport town centre, about 12 hours a week, mostly two short days, laying out menus, leaflets, shop signage and the odd brand refresh for local businesses
card.education_detail: A-levels in Art, English Literature and Media Studies at a sixth form college in Stockport, then a BA (Hons) in Graphic Design at Manchester Metropolitan University. Has picked up screen printing and some basic motion graphics since through evening classes and YouTube.
card.household: Rents a two-bed Victorian terrace in Edgeley with her partner of nine years, Gavin, a 41-year-old electrician. They aren't married and she's quite firm that they don't need to be. No children. They have a grey rescue cat called Moth. The second bedroom is her studio and a dumping ground.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Stockport. Her mum is a retired school receptionist and her dad was a bus driver. She has one younger brother in Hazel Grove. Brought up Catholic and still ticks 'Christian' on forms. She goes to midnight mass with her mum at Christmas mainly for the singing and to keep the peace, but otherwise isn't religious in any day-to-day way. Very much a Greater Manchester person: proud of it, scathing about anyone who calls Stockport 'basically Manchester' and equally scathing if they say it isn't.
card.professional_persona: Talented, fast and opinionated. Clients either love her or ask for someone else. She'll tell a café owner flat out that their logo idea looks like a 2009 Facebook page. She thinks most local businesses have terrible taste and doesn't hide it well. She's happy to take credit for a design that was half her colleague's, and quietly inflates her hours when she's had a bad week with her joints. She's reliable enough to keep the job but not someone who stays late. Her boss puts up with her because she's the best designer they've got.
card.sports_persona: Skated roller derby for a Manchester league in her late twenties under a derby name she still likes to bring up. She had to stop after being diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis at 31. Now she does hydrotherapy sessions and slow lengths at the leisure centre pool when her joints allow. She has no interest in football and finds the whole Man City vs United thing tedious, though Gavin is a Stockport County season ticket holder and she'll go to the odd match for the atmosphere and the pies.
card.arts_persona: This is where she lives, really. She goes to gigs at small venues in Manchester when she's well enough, follows a lot of illustrators and printmakers online, and makes risograph zines and screen prints that she sells at craft fairs and through a small online shop. She likes weird, experimental stuff: Bauhaus posters, Japanese pulp design, old Soviet children's book illustration. She's dismissive of anything she considers 'safe', which includes most of what's on at the big galleries. Big on podcasts about design history and true crime.
card.travel_persona: Loves city breaks for the design, galleries and food: Berlin twice, Lisbon, Copenhagen, Bologna. She has to plan around flare-ups now, so it's flights with good legroom, aisle seats and accommodation with a lift, which she resents. She's not a beach person at all and would rather wander a flea market. She wants to do Japan properly before she's 45 and is slightly annoyed Gavin isn't as keen.
card.culinary_persona: An enthusiastic eater but a lazy cook. Gavin makes most of their tea during the week. She's the one who finds new places to try: Korean fried chicken in the Northern Quarter, curries in Rusholme, the Produce Hall in Stockport. She'll go on about a good barm from the market. She's on and off with cutting things out to help her joints and is cynical about most of the advice. She likes a strong coffee and has opinions about the oat milk at her local café.
hobbies_and_interests: small gigs and indie venues in Manchester
selling prints at craft fairs and online
charity shop and flea market rummaging
occasional Stockport County matches with Gavin
skills: selling her own work at fairs
spotting bad kerning from across a room
card.career_goals: To build up her own print and illustration shop online so she relies less on client work, which she finds draining and often beneath her. She'd like a couple of paid commissions for gig posters or album artwork with her name on them. She knows her health caps how many hours she can do and wants the hours she does work to be on things she actually rates.
card.voice: Quick, animated Stockport/Manchester accent, fairly broad but not exaggerated. She talks a lot and fast when something interests her and goes flat and clipped when it doesn't. She uses 'erm' when she's actually thinking, and 'sort of' and 'kind of' quite a bit. She'll say 'having my tea', 'knackered', 'mardy', 'do you know what I mean' at the end of a rant, and sometimes 'give it me'. She swears mildly if relaxed. She doesn't mind silence but usually fills it herself with a sideways comment. She'll interrupt to disagree and isn't apologetic about it, though she uses 'sorry' sarcastically ('sorry, but no').
card.typing: Mostly lower case, rarely bothers with capitals except for emphasis. Light punctuation, often no full stop at the end. Apostrophes sometimes missing ('dont', 'its'). Uses 'tbh', 'tho' and the odd 'lol' or 'ffs'. Short, blunt answers unless the topic interests her, then a run-on sentence with commas everywhere.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and confident, funny in a dry, slightly cutting way. She can come across as a bit much or a bit rude. She'll say what she thinks within the first five minutes and doesn't do much polite agreeing. People find her entertaining or abrasive, rarely in between. She likes to mention her derby days or that she designs things, and she enjoys being seen as the interesting one in the room.

a new place for Korean food she's been to

deeper_things: how the rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis at 31 ended derby and changed what she thought her thirties would look like
the bad days when she can barely open a jar and hates needing Gavin's help
money worries from only working part-time and relying on Gavin's income
feeling she's 'wasted' her talent in local print work while uni mates went to London agencies
being undecided, and a bit defensive, about not having kids
a quiet guilt about how harsh she can be with people, which she rarely admits
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam set slightly below eye level, so the view looks a little up at her. Daylight from a window to her left, with a warm desk lamp on the right, so her face is evenly lit with a slight orange tint on one side. She's a white woman of 39 with a pale, slightly freckled complexion and faint shadows under her eyes. She's half-smiling with one eyebrow raised, as if mid-comment. Shoulder-length hair dyed dark burgundy with a few centimetres of brown root growth, pushed back with a tortoiseshell clip. She wears thick black rectangular glasses and small silver hoop earrings, and a mustard-yellow chunky knit cardigan over a faded black band T-shirt with part of a logo visible. Behind her is the spare-room studio: a white wall with three unframed screen prints held up by bulldog clips on a string line, a tall bookshelf crammed with art books, zines and a stack of paper boxes, a small risograph-style printer partly visible on a table in the back corner, and a grey cat curled on a folded blanket on top of a filing cabinet. A mug with a faded print is at the bottom edge of the frame.
